title: bug: release_task's and release_resource's force, documented as a governor/human crash-recovery override, is honoured from any worker or QA seat, and release_task's own refusals tell the refused seat to retry with force:true, so a seat can strip a live peer mid-step or drop every lease
description:
Filed by governor-e6b40560 from defect hunt #9's held-back item (a) (task-66961b32, architect-24611a0a, #governors msg-bb61da0b). The hunt passed it up as a design call. GOVERNOR RULING: force follows its documented audience, governor or human. This is the same reasoning as task-629ddc99 (the set_task_status role gate), and the human can veto by dragging this row to BACKLOG.

PROBLEM (moe/work-2026-10-24 at 39bec237 / a028ec65)
- release_task's force parameter is documented as "Governor/human crash-recovery override: release a row you do not hold, or one whose step is IN_PROGRESS" (src/tools/releaseTask.ts:104-107). release_resource's force says "Release regardless of ownership (governor/human intervention)", and without taskId it releases ALL leases and queue entries (src/tools/releaseResource.ts:22).
- Neither handler resolves the caller's role. src/util/claimGuards.ts assertNoLiveLease and assertReleaseCaller return early on `if (force) return;`. TOOL_AUDIENCE does not protect them either: it filters only the listing (McpAdapter.ts:270, "not a permission check").
- The refusals themselves point a refused seat at the override. STEP_LEASE_HELD says "pass force:true to override a confirmed-dead holder", and RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE says "pass force:true to release a row you do not hold" (claimGuards.ts, assertNoLiveLease and assertReleaseCaller).
- Siblings that gate in the handler: set_task_priority (governor), set_task_dependencies and amend_plan_step (architect/governor), and set_task_status once 629ddc99 lands. All use workerHasRole + notAllowed.

EVIDENCE
/mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-66961b32/B/zzHuntB_releaseTaskForceGate.test.ts, with its output in .vitest.txt beside it, on HEAD 39bec237 in a snapshot. Result: "Tests 2 failed | 3 passed".
- "refuses force:true from a worker seat on a live peer mid-step" and the same for a qa seat: each "promise resolved { success: true … } instead of rejecting".
- Controls pass: without force the same worker is refused RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE, and a governor seat and a workerId-less call may force.

WHO USES FORCE TODAY
No seat flow does:
- scripts/moe-agent.sh:9045 and :9063 say "never with force" / "Never force".
- No role doc or skill tells a worker or QA seat to pass force.
- The governor's crash-recovery release (governor.md escalation step 5) and the human/board path keep it.

FIX DIRECTION (the architect decides)
- When force is true and params.workerId is present, refuse unless workerHasRole(state, workerId, 'governor'), with notAllowed and no write. A workerId-less call stays allowed (the human/board path), the same carve-out 629ddc99 makes.
- Apply this to release_task and release_resource.
- Reword the two claimGuards refusals for a non-governor caller, e.g. "ask a governor (moe.release_task force is governor/human only)", instead of "pass force:true".
- Name the audience in both force descriptions.

Gate: narrow, per the epic-be924fb8 ruling msg-bbf4f109. Run the ported repro plus the releaseTask, releaseResource and claimGuards test files.
definitionOfDone: release_task with force:true from a worker- or qa- seat on a peer-held row (with or without an IN_PROGRESS step) is refused NOT_ALLOWED and writes nothing (assignee, step and lease unchanged); a governor seat and a workerId-less call can still force, and the ported hunt repro passes in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

release_resource with force:true from a worker- or qa- seat is refused NOT_ALLOWED and releases nothing; a governor seat and a workerId-less call can still force; a seat releasing its own lease without force behaves as before.
The RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE and STEP_LEASE_HELD refusals no longer tell a non-governor caller to pass force:true, and the existing releaseTask, releaseResource and claimGuards test files stay green.

- task-idle: WORKING, held by 'worker-peer2', step-1 COMPLETED and step-2 PENDING.

Cases, with these title prefixes:
- (p1) The release_task inputSchema force description still matches /^Governor\/human crash-recovery override/.
- (p2) worker-1 force:true on task-peer rejects with codeName NOT_ALLOWED. Afterwards the row is unchanged: [status, assignedWorkerId, step-1 status] is ['WORKING','worker-peer','IN_PROGRESS'].
- (p3) qa-1 force:true on task-peer rejects NOT_ALLOWED; the assignee is unchanged.
- (p4) qa-1 force:true on task-idle (no IN_PROGRESS step) rejects NOT_ALLOWED; the assignee is unchanged.
- (p5) governor-1 force on task-peer and a workerId-less force on task-idle both return success:true, and both assignees become null.
- (p6) A worker-1 release of task-peer without force rejects with codeName RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE. A workerId-less release of task-peer without force rejects with STEP_LEASE_HELD. Neither error message contains 'pass force:true', and both contain 'governor or a human'.
  - Type the caught errors: `await release(...).catch((e: unknown) => e) as MoeError`, with `import type { MoeError } from '../util/errors.js'`. The gate typechecks this file (TS18046 otherwise).
- (r1) worker-peer acquires 'gate' for task-peer via acquireResourceTool. Then worker-1 force:true with taskId task-peer and qa-1 force:true without taskId each reject NOT_ALLOWED, and the holders are still ['task-peer:worker-peer'].

- (r3) A workerId-less release_resource without force still rejects MISSING_REQUIRED. worker-peer releasing its own lease without force returns released ['task-peer'], as before.

Run the file in a snapshot before the fix and expect 6 failed | 3 passed (p1, p5 and r3 are controls). The architect dry-ran a draft of these cases. Edit with your own editing tool, never a shell write.

implementationPlan.description:
release_task gate plus the guard wording.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/releaseTask.ts:
- Import notAllowed from ../util/errors.js and workerHasRole from ../util/workerRole.js, the resolver the restricted siblings use (setTaskPriority.ts:47, setTaskDependencies.ts:69, amendPlanStep.ts:62).
- Directly after `const force = params.force === true;` add: if force && params.workerId && !workerHasRole(state, params.workerId, 'governor'), throw notAllowed('release_task', `force is the governor/human crash-recovery override (worker ${params.workerId} is not a governor)`).
- The rule is role-only, with no assignee exemption: the assignee never needs force for its own row, because assertReleaseCaller and assertNoLiveLease both pass the assignee.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/util/claimGuards.ts, reword the two refusal tails so neither tells the caller to pass force:true:
- assertNoLiveLease (STEP_LEASE_HELD): '...IN_PROGRESS; only a governor or a human may override that lease (moe.release_task force), and only for a confirmed-dead holder'.
- assertReleaseCaller (RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE): '...not <caller>; only the holder may release it, or a governor or a human (moe.release_task force) once the holder is confirmed dead'.
- Keep the codeNames, the MoeErrorCode and the context objects exactly as they are. claim_next_task's replaceExisting path shares the STEP_LEASE_HELD text, and the neutral wording suits it too.

implementationPlan.description:
release_resource gate.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/releaseResource.ts:
- Import notAllowed and workerHasRole.
- Schema `required` becomes ['resourceId']. A human's force call may omit workerId, which gives DoD 2's workerId-less force path. The proxy always injects a seat's MOE_WORKER_ID, so seats are always gated.
- Replace the missingRequired('workerId') check with `if (!params.workerId && params.force !== true) throw missingRequired('workerId')`.
- After the RESOURCE_ID_RE check: if params.force === true && params.workerId && !workerHasRole(state, params.workerId, 'governor'), throw notAllowed('release_resource', `force is the governor/human override (worker ${params.workerId} is not a governor)`).
- Then `if (params.workerId) await state.touchWorker(params.workerId)`.
- Pass `workerId: params.workerId ?? ''` to state.releaseResource. Under force, the store's matchesCaller (resourceStore.ts:319-323) matches by taskId or by every holder and never reads the caller id. Say so in a comment.
- Give the two `params.taskId ?? params.workerId` message fallbacks a final `?? 'every holder'`.
- Update the descriptions: the tool description says force is 'governor or human only'; the force description says a caller whose workerId resolves to no governor role is refused NOT_ALLOWED; the workerId description says 'required unless force:true from a human, who omits it'.

Error handling: both refusals are thrown before touchWorker, the precondition reads and the store write, so nothing is released and no lease or queue entry changes.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/releaseResource.generation.test.ts, case 'checks PEER leases too under force with no taskId' (line 137) forces as worker-1, which is now refused before its precondition. Switch that caller to 'governor-1'. Keep ifHolderWorkerId 'worker-1', the /worker-2/ rejection and the holders assertion. Add a one-line comment: since task-0adea941 only a governor or a human may force.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: force on moe.release_task and moe.release_resource follows its documented audience. A caller whose workerId resolves to no governor role (team role, else the id prefix, via workerHasRole) is refused NOT_ALLOWED before anything is read under the mutex or written. A governor seat and a workerId-less human or board call keep force. release_resource accepts a workerId-less call only with force:true. The RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE and STEP_LEASE_HELD refusals keep their codeNames but no longer tell the caller to pass force:true; they name a governor or a human as the override.
acceptanceCriteria: A release_task force from a worker- or qa- seat on a peer-held row, with or without an IN_PROGRESS step, rejects NOT_ALLOWED and leaves the status, assignee and step unchanged. Governor and workerId-less forces succeed.

A release_resource force from a worker- or qa- seat rejects NOT_ALLOWED and releases nothing. Governor and workerId-less forces release. An own-lease release without force is unchanged, and a workerId-less non-force call is still MISSING_REQUIRED.
Neither guard message contains 'pass force:true', and the releaseTask, releaseResource.generation, claimNextTask.race and resourceStore test files stay green.

The assignee releasing its own row or lease without force behaves exactly as before.

/ws RELEASE_TASK (no workerId, force forwarded) still forces.

issues.description: The truthy workerId gate lets a seat send workerId '' or null with force:true and strip a live mid-step peer (probe: success:true, assignee null). An id of 123 throws an uncoded TypeError. Gate on key presence the way setTaskStatus.ts:105 does: when force is set and `params.workerId !== undefined`, normalise a non-string id to '' and refuse unless workerHasRole(..., 'governor'). Keep the absent-key path allowed and the refusal before any read.

Same hole: workerId '' with force:true from a seat drops every lease (probe: released ['task-peer'], holders []). Apply the same key-presence gate. Keep line 39's MISSING_REQUIRED for a non-force call with no usable workerId, and call touchWorker (line 51) only for a non-blank string id. An absent-key force must still release.

Add cases that are red against 31492ac5. release_task force with workerId '' and with null must reject NOT_ALLOWED and leave the snapshot unchanged. Workerid 123 must reject NOT_ALLOWED, not a TypeError. release_resource force with workerId '' must reject NOT_ALLOWED and keep the holders. p5 and r2 stay green. You can port the cases from /mnt/d/moe-scratch/qa-0adea941/zzQaProbe.test.ts, then re-run the verification command unchanged.

rejectionHistory.reason:
Completion 31492ac5 is on moe/work-2026-10-24 and origin. The exact task.verification command re-ran green in a snapshot of HEAD 31492ac5: exit 0, 10 files, 157 tests. The diff is +191/-22, in scope, and otherwise clean.

The rejection is for DoD 1 and DoD 2. Both gates treat a PRESENT-but-blank workerId as the human path: `force && params.workerId && ...` at releaseTask.ts:145 and releaseResource.ts:45. moe-proxy injects MOE_WORKER_ID only when the workerId KEY is absent (moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:234). So a worker or QA seat that sends `workerId: ""` or `null` with force:true still forces.

I probed it in the same snapshot with /mnt/d/moe-scratch/qa-0adea941/zzQaProbe.test.ts:
- release_task {workerId:'', force:true} on task-peer (step-1 IN_PROGRESS) returned success:true with releasedBy 'unknown', and the assignee became null. null gives the same result.
- release_resource {workerId:'', force:true} returned released ['task-peer'] and left holders [].
- workerId:123 with force throws an uncoded TypeError (workerId.startsWith) instead of NOT_ALLOWED.

The task description asks for "the same carve-out 629ddc99 makes", which is key-based. setTaskStatus.ts:105 at base 14126ecd gates on `params.workerId !== undefined` and normalises a non-string id to ''. The absent-key human, /ws board and moe-call.sh paths stay allowed, and no legitimate caller sends a blank key. Your step-5 note flagged this as theoretical. The new force description, "a human or the board omits workerId", points a refused seat one step from trying it.
